rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet’s first prayer toward the Kaaba was Ẓuhr, which was the middle prayer.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر: أن أول صلاة صلاها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الكعبة صلاة الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well-known account makes the first prayer toward the Kaaba ʿAṣr, explaining why the people of Qubāʾ heard the news only by Fajr.
rows.anchor: والمشهور أن أول صلاة صلاها إلى الكعبة صلاة العصر، ولهذا تأخر الخبر عن أهل قباء إلى صلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: نويلة بنت مسلم
rows.claim: Nuwayla reports that worshippers at Banū Ḥāritha, facing Jerusalem in Ẓuhr or ʿAṣr, turned toward the Kaaba after hearing the Prophet had done so, and completed the prayer in the new direction.
rows.anchor: عن جدته أم أبيه نويلة بنت مسلم، قالت: صلينا الظهر -أو العصر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man of Banū Ḥāritha reports that the Prophet praised those who changed direction during prayer as men who believe in the unseen.
rows.anchor: فحدثني رجل من بني حارثة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عمارة بن أوس
rows.claim: ʿUmāra ibn Aws reports that a caller announced the qibla change while they were bowing toward Jerusalem, and the imam, men, and boys turned toward the Kaaba while still bowing.
rows.anchor: عن عمارة بن أوس قال: بينما نحن في الصلاة نحو بيت المقدس، ونحن ركوع، إذ أتى مناد بالباب

words: وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنتُمْ فَوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command requires facing the Kaaba from every direction on earth: east, west, north, and south.
rows.anchor: أمر تعالى باستقبال الكعبة من جميع جهات الأرض، شرقا وغربا وشمالا وجنوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A traveler may perform voluntary prayer facing whichever way the mount or body turns, while keeping the heart oriented toward the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: سوى النافلة في حال السفر، فإنه يصليها حيثما توجه قالبه، وقلبه نحو الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In combat with weapons, a worshipper prays in whatever condition is possible.
rows.anchor: وكذا في حال المسايفة في القتال يصلي على كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone unable to identify the qibla prays after exercising judgment; even if mistaken, this is excused because God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
rows.anchor: من جهل جهة القبلة يصلي باجتهاده، وإن كان مخطئا في نفس الأمر، لأن الله تعالى لا يكلف نفسا إلا وسعها

rows.speaker: المالكية
rows.claim: The Mālikīs infer that a worshipper looks straight ahead, since looking at the place of prostration would require bending and impair full upright posture.
rows.anchor: قال المالكية لقوله: {فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام} فلو نظر إلى موضع سجوده

rows.speaker: الشافعي وأحمد وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and Abū Ḥanīfa hold that the worshipper looks at the place of prostration while standing, contrary to the Mālikī view.
rows.anchor: كما ذهب إليه الشافعي وأحمد وأبو حنيفة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some authorities say the worshipper looks toward the chest while standing.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: ينظر المصلي في قيامه إلى صدره

rows.speaker: شريك القاضي
rows.claim: Sharīk al-Qāḍī agrees with the majority that one looks at the place of prostration when standing, since this better promotes humility and is supported by a hadith.
rows.anchor: وقال شريك القاضي: ينظر في حال قيامه إلى موضع سجوده

rows.speaker: شريك القاضي
rows.claim: Sharīk assigns the gaze to the feet in bowing, the nose in prostration, and the lap while sitting.
rows.anchor: وأما في حال ركوعه فإلى موضع قدميه، وفي حال سجوده إلى موضع أنفه وفي حال قعوده إلى حجره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews who objected to the Kaaba direction knew God would direct the Prophet to it: their scriptures described the Prophet and his community and foretold his uniquely complete, honored law. They concealed this knowledge from envy, disbelief, and obstinacy, so God threatens them.
rows.anchor: أي: واليهود -الذين أنكروا استقبالكم الكعبة وانصرافكم عن بيت المقدس -يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tests believers through ease and hardship, including fear and hunger; the cited likeness of hunger and fear to clothing reflects how visibly each affects a person.
rows.anchor: أي: يختبرهم ويمتحنهم، كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘something of fear and hunger’ means a little of each.
rows.anchor: أي: بقليل من ذلك {ونقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss of wealth means losing some of it; loss of lives includes the deaths of companions, relatives, and loved ones; loss of fruits means gardens and farms yield less than usual.
rows.anchor: كموت الأصحاب والأقارب والأحباب {والثمرات} أي: لا تغل الحدائق

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities said that in the trial some palm trees bore only one fruit.
rows.anchor: كما قال بعض السلف: فكانت بعض النخيل لا تثمر غير واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These and similar events test God’s servants: the patient are rewarded, while those who despair incur punishment.
rows.anchor: الذين شكرهم، قال: {الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة قالوا إنا لله

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes take fear as fear of God, hunger as Ramadan fasting, loss of wealth as almsgiving, loss of lives as illness, and loss of fruits as children; Ibn Kathīr considers this interpretation questionable.
rows.anchor: وقد حكى بعض المفسرين أن المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient console themselves with this confession: they belong to God, who disposes of His servants as He wills, and return to Him in the afterlife, where not even an atom’s weight is lost; this acknowledges their servanthood and return.
rows.anchor: أي: تسلوا بقولهم هذا عما أصابهم، وعلموا أنهم ملك لله يتصرف في عبيده

words: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَٰتٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ṣalawāt upon the patient means His praise of them and mercy.
rows.anchor: أي: ثناء من الله عليهم ورحمة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr interprets the ṣalawāt as security from punishment.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: أي أمنة من العذاب

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar calls the prayers and mercy the two packed loads, and guidance the extra placed between them, a further reward for the patient.
rows.anchor: قال أمير المؤمنين عمر بن الخطاب: نعم العدلان ونعمت العلاوة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In Aḥmad’s report from Umm Salama, the Prophet promises that anyone struck by calamity who says the return formula and asks God to reward them and replace the loss with something better will receive that answer.
rows.anchor: سمعت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قولا سررت به

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Umm Salama reports that after Abū Salama died she made the prescribed supplication, doubting anyone could be better; after her waiting period the Prophet married her, addressed her concerns about jealousy, age, and dependents, and she regarded him as God’s better replacement.
rows.anchor: قالت أم سلمة: فحفظت ذلك منه، فلما توفي أبو سلمة استرجعت وقلت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Muslim also transmits from Umm Salama the Prophet’s promise of divine reward and a better replacement for one who makes this supplication after calamity; she says it was fulfilled after Abū Salama’s death.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم، عنها أنها قالت: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī reports the Prophet’s promise that a Muslim who remembers an old calamity and renews the return formula receives anew the equivalent of the original reward; Aḥmad and Ibn Mājah transmit it, with variants in its chain wording.
rows.anchor: عن أبيها الحسين بن علي، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā reports a divine saying: when a servant praises God and says the return formula after losing a child, God commands a house in Paradise called the House of Praise; al-Tirmidhī grades the report ḥasan gharīb.
rows.anchor: عن أبي موسى، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī calls the report about the House of Praise ḥasan gharīb and identifies Abū Sinān as ʿĪsā ibn Sinān.
rows.anchor: وقال: حسن غريب. واسم أبي سنان: عيسى بن سنان

rows.speaker: أعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Ḥātim reports that a Bedouin asked whether the Lord was near, so they could whisper, or distant, so they should call aloud; the Prophet was silent and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن جده، أن أعرابيا قال: يا رسول الله، أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the Companions asked the Prophet where their Lord was, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: سأل أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports that after 40:60 was revealed, people asked when they should supplicate, and this verse followed.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج عن عطاء: أنه بلغه لما نزلت

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā reports that during a campaign the Prophet told the Companions to lower their voices: they call one who hears and sees, not one deaf or absent, and is nearer than a rider’s mount’s neck; he then taught them that there is no might or power except through God, a treasure of Paradise. The report is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and other collections.
rows.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري، قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزاة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet quoted God as saying, ‘I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he calls upon Me.’
rows.anchor: حدثنا شعبة، حدثنا قتادة، عن أنس رضي الله عنه: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports God’s promise to be with His servant while the servant remembers Him and moves his lips in remembrance.
rows.anchor: عن كريمة بنت الخشخاش المزنية، قالت: حدثنا أبو هريرة: أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr links this assurance of divine company to God’s being with the pious and doers of good, and His promise to Moses and Aaron to hear and see them.
rows.anchor: قلت: وهذا كقوله تعالى: {إن الله مع الذين اتقوا والذين هم محسنون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not disappoint a supplicant or become distracted from the prayer; He hears supplication. The verse encourages prayer, which is never lost with Him.
rows.anchor: والمراد من هذا: أنه تعالى لا يخيب دعاء داع، ولا يشغله عنه شيء

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
rows.claim: Salman reports the Prophet’s statement that God is too generous to return a servant’s raised hands empty after the servant asks Him for good. Al-Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan gharīb; some transmitters did not raise it to the Prophet, and other collections transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن سلمان -يعني الفارسي -رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports that a Muslim’s lawful prayer, without a break of kinship, receives one of three outcomes: swift fulfillment, preservation for the afterlife, or an equivalent harm averted; the Prophet says God gives abundantly.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit reports that a Muslim’s prayer is answered or an equivalent harm is kept away, provided it involves neither sin nor breaking family ties.
rows.anchor: عن مكحول، عن جبير بن نفير، أن عبادة بن الصامت حدثهم أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī grades the report from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb by this route.
rows.anchor: ورواه الترمذي، عن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن الدارمي

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that a servant continues to receive an answer so long as he is not impatient, saying, ‘I prayed, but my prayer was not answered.’ The report is in both Ṣaḥīḥs.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Muslim reports that prayer continues to be answered unless it asks for sin or severing kinship, or the servant grows impatient; impatience is repeating that one prayed without seeing an answer, then tiring of prayer and abandoning it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet’s statement that a servant remains in a good state unless he becomes impatient, which means saying that he prayed but God did not answer.
rows.anchor: عن أنس: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha says a believer’s prayer either comes quickly in this life or is stored for the next, unless the person is impatient or despairing; she defines both as saying they asked but received no answer. ʿUrwa narrates her explanation.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها، أنها قالت: ما من عبد مؤمن يدعو الله بدعوة فتذهب، حتى تعجل له في الدنيا أو تدخر له في الآخرة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Ibn Qusayṭ says he heard Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib teach exactly what ʿĀʾisha taught about a prayer’s fulfillment, unless the supplicant is impatient or despairing.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قسيط: وسمعت سعيد بن المسيب يقول كقول عائشة سواء

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr reports the Prophet’s analogy of hearts as vessels, some more receptive than others, and urges people to ask with certainty: God does not answer a servant who calls with a heedless heart.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: نافع بن معد يكرب
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh transmits an unusual report from Nāfiʿ ibn Maʿd Yakrib: he and ʿĀʾisha asked about the verse, and Gabriel conveyed God’s greeting and promise to answer the sincere servant’s call. Ibn Kathīr calls this route gharīb.
rows.anchor: حدثني أبي نافع بن معد يكرب، قال: كنت أنا وعائشة سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الآية

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports through Ibn ʿAbbās from Jābir that the Prophet recited the verse and made a long talbiya affirming God’s oneness, the truth of the promise and meeting, Paradise, Hell, the Hour, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس: حدثني جابر بن عبد الله أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Al-Bazzār reports from Anas through al-Ḥasan that God assigns worship without partners to Himself, recompenses the servant’s deeds, and makes prayer the shared matter whose answer is His part.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، عن أنس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this encouragement to pray is placed amid the fasting rulings, Ibn Kathīr reads it as urging earnest supplication after completing the fast month and at every ifṭār.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية الباعثة على الدعاء، متخللة بين أحكام الصيام، إرشاد إلى الاجتهاد في الدعاء

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr reports that a fasting person has an answered prayer at ifṭār; he would gather his family and children to pray when breaking the fast.
rows.anchor: عن جده عبد الله بن عمرو، قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Mājah transmits from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr that the fasting person’s supplication at breaking the fast is not refused; Ibn Abī Mulayka heard him ask for forgiveness by God’s all-encompassing mercy.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن عمرو، قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet names three supplications that are not rejected: those of a just ruler, a fasting person until ifṭār, and an oppressed person. The last rises beneath the clouds, heaven’s gates open for it, and God vows to grant help even if delayed; the report appears in Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, and Ibn Mājah.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوْا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the opponents stop fighting in the sanctuary and turn to Islam and repentance, God forgives their sins, even if they killed Muslims in His sanctuary; no sin is too great for Him to forgive when one repents.
rows.anchor: أي: فإن تركوا القتال في الحرم، وأنابوا إلى الإسلام والتوبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وأبو العالية، ومجاهد، والحسن، وقتادة، والربيع، ومقاتل بن حيان، والسدي، وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ, Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, al-Suddī, and Zayd ibn Aslam say fitna here means shirk.
rows.anchor: أي: شرك. قاله ابن عباس، وأبو العالية، ومجاهد، والحسن، وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religion being for God means His religion becomes manifest and exalted above all other religions.
rows.anchor: ويكون الدين لله} أي: يكون دين الله هو الظاهر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report in both Ṣaḥīḥs, the Prophet says the one who fights so God’s word is supreme is fighting in God’s path, distinguishing this aim from courage, partisanship, and display.
rows.anchor: كما ثبت في الصحيحين: عن أبي موسى الأشعري، قال: سئل النبي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in both Ṣaḥīḥs says the Prophet was commanded to fight until people profess God’s oneness; then their blood and property are protected except by right, and their account is with God.
rows.anchor: أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا: لا إله إلا الله، فإذا قالوها عصموا مني دماءهم وأموالهم إلا بحقها
